b.d: Procter & Gamble's European and worldwide laundry detergent brand, developed in Belgium and launched in 1967.
Scouring-powder brand made by SerVaas Laboratories in Indianapolis.
Arçelik's international appliance brand; budget front-loaders such as the RecycledTub range.
Grand Rapids carpet-sweeper firm turned maker of uprights, hand vacs and carpet washers.
Tool maker whose 1979 Dustbuster defined the cordless handheld vacuum.
Procter & Gamble laundry detergent, launched in the UK in 1974 and relaunched in 1982 as a combined detergent and conditioner.
Bosch home-appliance brand (BSH) with Unlimited cordless sticks; its power-tool arm sells AdvancedVac wet-dry vacuums.
Privately owned Dutch housewares maker of waste bins, laundry racks and ironing boards.
German design-led consumer products company; household line includes CareStyle steam generator irons.
US dishwasher detergent brand sold as ActionPacs, gel and powder, plus rinse aid.
Oakland company best known for chlorine bleach, owner of several US cleaning brands.
American small-appliance and personal-care company based in Stamford, Connecticut; a major US garment-steamer seller.
John Corby Ltd began making valet stands in Windsor in 1930; its electric trouser press became the generic name and a hotel-room fixture.
Procter & Gamble dish detergent brand for the US market.
UK laundry detergent launched in 1953 by Procter & Gamble and acquired by Bluesun in 2024.
Reckitt antiseptic and disinfectant brand that began with Dettol antiseptic liquid; sold worldwide except the United States.
Unilever bleach-based cleaning brand first made by Wilfred Handley in Newcastle upon Tyne.
S. C. Johnson drain-cleaner brand that began with Crystal Drano.
Suzhou maker, Xiaomi-backed, of L and X series robot vacuum-mops and V/Z cordless sticks.
James Dyson's cyclonic vacuum company, founded in Malmesbury and now headquartered in Singapore.
Maker of liquidless laundry detergent sheets tested by Consumer Reports.
Suzhou robotics company behind the Deebot floor robots and Winbot window robots.
Plant- and mineral-based cleaning brand from Malle, owned by S. C. Johnson since 2017 alongside Method.
Landau an der Isar tool maker selling TC-AV ash vacuums and wet-dry vacs.
Stockholm appliance group; front-loaders with LuxCare wash and stacked laundry centres; owns Frigidaire and AEG.
Anker's smart-home brand selling RoboVac and Omni robot vacuums.
Procter & Gamble washing-up liquid and dishwasher brand, sold as Dreft, Yes or Jar in some countries.
Reckitt dishwasher brand begun by Economics Laboratory; formerly Electrasol and Calgonit in some markets.
Auckland appliance maker; SmartDrive direct-drive top-loaders (WashSmart, QuickSmart).
American appliance brand of Electrolux; top-load laundry centres and budget washers.
Louisville appliance maker owned by Haier; Profile front- and top-loaders, UltraFast heat-pump combos and Unitized Spacemaker laundry centres.
Premium line of GE Appliances of Louisville, Kentucky, owned by Haier since 2016.
British cleaning and waterproofing brand for outdoor clothing, footwear and equipment, trading since 1937.
Qingdao appliance group; I-Pro Series 7 front-loaders in Europe, twin-tubs in Japan; owns GE Appliances, Candy and Hoover.
Reckitt toilet-cleaner brand named after its inventor Harry Pickup, sold worldwide.
Qingdao white-goods and electronics group; A-rated budget front-loaders in Europe.
Japanese group whose home-appliance arm still sells Aozora (青空) twin-tub washers in Japan.
Ohio pioneer of the electric upright, so dominant that 'hoover' became the British word for vacuuming; now split between Haier (Europe) and TTI (North America).
Sendai-based Japanese housewares and small-appliance maker; its Kararie futon dryers lead Japanese sales rankings.
Massachusetts robotics firm that created the Roomba in 2002 and the Braava mopping robots.

b.d: London design-led houseware brand founded by twins Richard and Antony Joseph; Glide and Pocket ironing boards.
Costco's private label launched in 1995; its Ultra Clean laundry detergent is a Consumer Reports best-value pick.
German cleaning-machine maker whose WD wet-and-dry drums, AD ash vacuums and RC robots are household standards.
Swiss maker of high-end ironing systems and steam generators, founded by Jean Monney; connected Laurastar Smart launched 2017.
German household-products maker from Nassau for cleaning, laundry and ironing, listed in Frankfurt since 1984.
Korean electronics group selling CordZero cordless sticks with Kompressor bin compaction and auto-empty towers.
Reckitt disinfectant brand, the US counterpart to Dettol.
Newton, Iowa laundry brand now part of Whirlpool; heavy-duty top-loaders with Pet Pro and Extra Power options.
San Francisco maker of biodegradable natural cleaning and laundry products, bought by Ecover in 2012.
German appliance maker whose bagged cylinders and Triflex sticks are long-standing test favourites.
Trading name of Vale Mill (Rochdale); took on ironing boards in 1987 via the Relax Ironing Board Company, still made in Rochdale.
Japanese electronics group making high-end home appliances including Pokasara futon dryers.
British electrical-appliance brand from Swinton, South Yorkshire, now manufactured in the Far East.
S. C. Johnson hard-surface cleaner brand that began with an aerosol oven cleaner.
Procter & Gamble all-purpose cleaner brand, sold as Flash in the UK and Meister Proper, Monsieur Propre or Mastro Lindo elsewhere.
British maker of water-based cleaning and waterproofing products for outdoor clothing and gear, started by Nick Brown in 1977.
Copenhagen cleaning-equipment group with the Buddy consumer wet-dry range.
Somerset maker of the smiling-faced Henry cylinder vacuum and its related George wet-dry and Henry Quick stick models.
Osaka-based electronics manufacturer, a long-standing maker of futon dryers.
Laundry detergent brand owned by Henkel and licensed to Unilever in the UK and Ireland; introduced 1907.
Dutch electronics group whose garment-care line spans Azur steam irons, PerfectCare steam generators and handheld steamers.
Italian maker of household steam appliances, known for the Vaporetto high-pressure boiler steam cleaner and the Vaporella boiler iron.
Beijing robot-vacuum maker launched with Xiaomi backing; now a premium robot brand.
German small-appliance brand, part of Groupe SEB since 1988, with a long history of electric and steam irons.
Carpet-cleaning machine brand, now Rug Doctor by Bissell, selling and renting deep carpet cleaners and spot cleaners for home use.
British household-appliance brand, kettle pioneer, with wide steam iron, steam generator and Steam Genie steamer ranges.
Korean electronics group whose Bespoke Jet sticks and Jet Bot robots compete at the premium end.
3M brand of stain and water repellent for fabrics, discovered by accident in 1953 and sold since 1956.
Velbert maker (Stein & Co) of durable bagged uprights and cylinders for homes and commercial cleaning.
Burlington, Vermont company selling eco-friendly laundry detergent, dish soap and household products; owned by Unilever since 2016.
SharkNinja's vacuum brand, launched 2007, known for Lift-Away uprights and cordless sticks.
Williamsport maker whose name became the generic term for workshop wet-dry vacuums; now owned by GreatStar.
UK letterbox subscription brand for dishwasher tablets, laundry capsules and fabric conditioner.
Henkel brand launched as Germany's first detergent made specifically for dishwashers, first sold as a powder.
Ripon, Wisconsin laundry-machine maker known for agitator top-loaders with long warranties, sold by Alliance Laundry Systems.
Stockholm clothing-care brand founded in Sweden in 2014 (co-founder Frej Lewenhaupt); known for Cirrus handheld steamers.
British Unilever laundry detergent brand sold worldwide since 1952 (Henkel-owned in North America).
Groupe SEB brand (T-fal in North America) making steam irons, Pro Express steam generators and Access Steam steamers.
Procter & Gamble's US laundry detergent brand since 1946; Tide Pods popularised capsule detergent in 2012.
Chinese cordless-stick and floor-washer maker known for Pure One smart vacuums.
British floorcare brand (TTI group) selling cordless sticks, uprights and carpet washers.
Freudenberg Group cleaning and laundry brand, started with the Vileda Window Cloth in 1948; makes Total Reflect ironing boards.
Benton Harbor appliance group; top-load and front-load washers plus compact laundry centres; owns Maytag.
S. C. Johnson glass and hard-surface cleaner brand.
Osaka-based maker of vacuum flasks, rice cookers and small appliances including Smart Dry futon dryers.
Ohio maker of metal-bodied upright vacuums sold by home demonstration.
German household-appliance maker whose Kobold upright vacuum dates from 1929.
Troy, Michigan maker of the Rainbow water-filter vacuum cleaner.
